record.final_answer:
**The total shipping cost for October is 58.01** across 6 orders.

| Order | Zone | Cost |
|---|---|---|
| A-1001 | north | 6.94 |
| A-1002 | south | 6.28 |
| A-1003 | island | 15.25 |
| A-1004 | north | 15.10 |
| A-1005 | south | 9.03 |
| A-1006 | north | 5.41 |

The script failed on the first run with `no rate for zone "north"`. The cause is that `data/zone-rates.tsv` uses Windows line endings, so the script read the zone names with a hidden character on the end (`north\r`) and none of them matched the orders.

I didn't change the script or either data file. The script takes an optional second argument for the rates file, so I gave it a temporary copy with the line endings removed. The rates themselves are the same. I checked one order by hand: A-1001 is 4.90 + 0.85 × 2.4 = 6.94, which matches.

If you want the script to work on its own, the rates file needs converting to normal line endings, for example with `dos2unix data/zone-rates.tsv`. I left that for you since you asked me not to touch it. I also saved a note about this problem to memory so a later session can work around it quickly.
